Une longue plage de sable bordée de coco: A long sandy beach lined with coconut palms, where the Mono River flows into the ocean. The village retains its 19th-century Afro-Brazilian character, and the lagoon just behind it can be explored by boat.
Novembre à mars, quand la mer est la plu: November to March, when the sea is at its calmest and the air at its driest.
La Bouche du Roy, l’embouchure du Mono e: La Bouche du Roy, the mouth of the River Mono and its sandbanks
Une sortie en pirogue dans la mangrove,: An early-morning canoe trip through the mangroves
Le site de ponte des tortues marines, en: The sea turtle nesting site, in season
La ville la plus chargée d’histoire du l: The coastal town steeped in history: a former slave port, the spiritual capital of vodoun, and a major site of remembrance. The Slave Route stretches for nearly four kilometres, linking the town to the beach.
Le 10 janvier pour la fête nationale du: On 10 January for the National Day of Vodoun; otherwise, all year round.
La Porte du Non-Retour, au bout de la Ro: The Gate of No Return, at the end of the Slave Route
Le Temple des Pythons, face à la basiliq: The Temple of the Pythons, opposite the basilica
Le musée installé dans l’ancien fort por: The museum housed in the former Portuguese fort
La forêt sacrée de Kpassè et ses statues: The sacred forest of Kpassè and its statues
La capitale économique, bruyante et dens: The bustling, densely populated economic capital, wedged between the ocean and Lake Nokoué. It is the country’s gateway: everything comes in and goes out through it.
Toute l’année. Les soirées de saison sèc: All year round. Evenings during the dry season are the most pleasant.
Le marché Dantokpa, l’un des plus grands: Dantokpa Market, one of the largest in West Africa
La Fondation Zinsou et la scène d’art co: The Zinsou Foundation and the contemporary art scene
La plage de Fidjrossè et ses paillotes,: Fidjrossè beach and its beach huts, in the evening
Une cité entièrement bâtie sur pilotis a: A town built entirely on stilts in the middle of Lake Nokoué, founded by the Tofinu to escape raids. Tens of thousands of people live there, travelling and trading by canoe.
Toute l’année ; partez tôt pour éviter l: All year round; set off early to avoid the heat on the water.
Le marché flottant, en fin de matinée: The floating market, late in the morning
La traversée depuis l’embarcadère d’Abom: The crossing from the Abomey-Calavi jetty
La capitale politique, plus calme que Co: The political capital, which is quieter than Cotonou, has an old town centre where Afro-Brazilian architecture, the royal palace and colonial houses stand side by side. It is the country’s museum capital.
Toute l’année ; les musées ferment souve: All year round; museums often close in the early afternoon.
Le musée Honmé, ancien palais du roi Tof: The Honmé Museum, the former palace of King Toffa
La Grande Mosquée, ancienne église de st: The Great Mosque, a former church built in the Afro-Brazilian style
Le musée Da Silva et le Jardin des plant: The Da Silva Museum and the Botanical Gardens
Un grand lac peu profond entouré de vill: A large, shallow lake surrounded by fishing villages. Possotomè, on the eastern shore, is known for its mineral springs and for the generally leisurely pace of life there.
Décembre à mars, hors des grandes pluies: December to March, outside the main rainy season.
Les techniques de pêche traditionnelles: The traditional fishing techniques of the Pédah people
Le marché de Bopa, sur l’autre rive: The Bopa market, on the opposite bank
Une des plus anciennes cités yoruba de l: One of the oldest Yoruba cities in the region, long surrounded by ramparts. The city remains the seat of a living monarchy and boasts a packed calendar of festivals.
Pendant les fêtes traditionnelles, entre: During the traditional festivals, between March and June.
La porte d’Akaba Idéna, vestige de l’enc: The Akaba Idéna Gate, a remnant of the fortified wall
Les masques Guèlèdè, inscrits au patrimo: Guèlèdè masks, listed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list
Une dépression argileuse entre Abomey et: A clay depression between Abomey and Cotonou, home to the last large tract of dense semi-deciduous forest in the south of the country, the heart of which is protected.
Saison sèche, quand les pistes restent p: The dry season, when the tracks remain passable.
Le noyau central de forêt naturelle: The central core of the natural forest
Les singes à ventre rouge, endémiques de: Red-bellied monkeys, which are endemic to the region
Les plantations de teck qui ceinturent l: The teak plantations that surround the reserve
Capitale du royaume du Dahomey pendant p: Capital of the Kingdom of Dahomeyfor nearly three centuries. Twelve kings reigned there in succession, each adding their own mud-brick palace to the same compound — a site listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Toute l’année ; visite guidée vivement c: Open all year round; a guided tour is highly recommended.
Les palais royaux et le musée historique: The royal palaces and the history museum
Les bas-reliefs polychromes racontant le: The polychrome bas-reliefs depicting the reigns
Le quartier des artisans : tentures appl: The craftsmen’s quarter: appliqué work, blacksmithing, weaving
Une ville posée au milieu d’un chaos de: A town nestled amidst a jumble of granite hills — forty-one, they say. It is also the country’s major Catholic place of pilgrimage.
Mi-août pour le pèlerinage national ; le: Mid-August for the national pilgrimage; the rest of the year for peace and quiet.
La grotte mariale d’Arigbo et son pèleri: The Marian grotto at Arigbo and its August pilgrimage
La montée sur les collines au lever du j: The climb up the hills at daybreak
Le palais du roi de Dassa: The palace of the King of Dassa
La grande ville du centre-nord et le car: The major city of the north-central region and the commercial hub between the south of the country and the Sahel. As the historic terminus of the railway, it pulsates to the rhythm of lorries and markets.
Toute l’année ; très chaud en mars-avril: All year round; very hot in March and April.
Le marché Arzèkè et ses tisserands: The Arzèkè market and its weavers
Capitale historique du royaume baatonou: The historic capital of the Baatonou (Bariba) kingdom, famous for its cavalry. La Gaani, its great festival, brings together hundreds of horsemen in full regalia around the king.
À la Gaani, dont la date suit le calendr: On Gaani, the date of which follows the Islamic lunar calendar.
La fête de la Gaani et sa cavalcade: The Gaani Festival and its parade
La cour royale et ses griots: The royal court and its griots
Ville marchande de l’ouest, longtemps ét: A trading town in the west, long a stopping point on the caravan routes between the Sahel and the coast. Craftsmanship here has remained a genuine trade, not merely a demonstration.
Novembre à février, pendant la saison sè: November to February, during the dry season.
Le grand marché, tous les cinq jours: The big market, every five days
La vieille ville et ses mosquées: The old town and its mosques
Une cascade encaissée dans les rochers à: A waterfall nestled amongst the rocks, about twenty kilometres from Natitingou, surrounded by dense vegetation. There is a natural pool below.
Juillet à octobre pour le débit ; la pis: July to October for the flow; the track is harder when it’s raining heavily.
Le bassin au pied de la chute: The pool at the foot of the waterfall
Le sentier d’approche à travers les roch: The approach path through the rocks
Le point de vue sur la vallée depuis le: The view of the valley from above
Le pays des Betammaribe, où l’on constru: The land of the Betammaribe, where tata somba are built: multi-storey earthen fortress-houses, with granaries, a terrace and a stable on the ground floor. The Koutammakou Cultural Landscape, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stretches on both sides of the Togolese border.
Novembre à février ; le marché vaut à lu: November to February; the market alone is worth a visit.
Une tata somba habitée, visitée avec la: A tata somba, visited with the family whilst it was still inhabited
Le marché de Boukoumbé, tous les quatre: The Boukoumbé market, held every four days
Les champs de fonio et de sorgho en terr: Terraced fields of fonio and sorghum
La porte d’entrée du Nord, adossée à la: The northern gateway, nestled against the Atacora mountain range. This is where the trails to Pendjari, the tata somba and the waterfalls begin.
Décembre à mai, la saison des circuits d: December to May: the tour season in the North.
Le panorama sur la chaîne depuis les hau: The view of the mountain range from the heights
Le marché et les points de départ vers l: The market and the departure points for Pendjari
Une chute d’eau à plusieurs paliers au p: A multi-tiered waterfall at the foot of the Atacora, on the road to Pendjari. You can walk up through the successive pools.
Août à novembre, quand la chute est plei: August to November, when the waterfall is at its fullest.
La montée vers les paliers supérieurs: The climb to the upper levels
L’arrêt sur la route du parc, en fin de: A stop on the way to the park, at the end of the day
La grande réserve du pays, environ 2 750: The country’s largest reserve, covering some 2,750 km² of wooded savannah at the foot of the Atacora Mountains. It is one of the last refuges for lions in West Africa, and a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
Décembre à mai. Le parc ferme en général: December to May. The park is usually closed during the rainy season.
Les mares à hippopotames et les points d: Hippopotamus pools and watering holes at dawn
Les lions et les guépards, avec de la pa: Lions and cheetahs – with a bit of patience
La part béninoise du complexe transfront: The Beninese section of the W Transboundary Site, shared with Niger and Burkina Faso, and listed as a World Heritage Site. Its name derives from the double meander of the River Niger.
Décembre à mai ; accès réglementé, guide: December to May; restricted access, guided tours compulsory.
Les rives du Niger et de la Mékrou: The banks of the Niger and the Mékrou
La ville la plus au nord, sur la rive du: The northernmost town, situated on the banks of the River Niger opposite the neighbouring country. Its weekly market attracts traders from across the sub-region.
Novembre à février, avant les grosses ch: November to February, before the heat of summer.
Le marché du dimanche, l’un des plus gra: The Sunday market, one of the largest in the North
Les rizières irriguées de la vallée: The irrigated rice fields of the valley
Les berges du Niger au coucher du soleil: The banks of the Niger at sunset
Le berceau : c’est d’Allada que sont par: The cradle: it was from Allada that the founders of Abomey and Porto-Novo set out in the 17<sup>th</sup> century. The Adja-Fon Kingdom left behind a palace, sacred forests and a lake where people still come to make offerings.
Toute l’année. Le 10 janvier, fête natio: All year round. 10 January: National vodoun Day.
Le palais royal et la cour du roi d’Alla: The Royal Palace and the Court of the King of Allada
Le lac sacré d’Awouto et ses légbas de b: The sacred lake of Awouto and its wooden légbas
Le monument au père de Toussaint Louvert: The monument to the father of Toussaint Louverture, who was born here
Le grand marché, un jour sur cinq: The big market, one day in five
Le site dit « des hommes à queue » : un: The site known as ‘the men with tails’: a network of tunnels dug into the laterite, which, according to tradition, were created by a people of blacksmiths who took refuge underground. Traces of iron mining are still visible on the walls.
Saison sèche, de novembre à mars : les g: Dry season, from November to March: the trails are more accessible.
Les galeries souterraines, avec un guide: The underground tunnels, with a guide from the village
Les scories de fer laissées par les fond: The iron slag left behind by the smelters
La case d’accueil et le récit des ancien: The welcome hut and the elders’ stories
Le marché de Dogbo et les palmeraies du: The Dogbo market and the palm groves of Couffo
Capitale du royaume mahi, adossée à ses: The capital of the Mahi Kingdom, nestled against the hills. The Gbaguidi dynasty has reigned here since the <sup>18th</sup> century, and the yam festival in August is one of the most popular in the country.
Mi-août pour la fête de l’igname ; le re: Mid-August for the yam festival; the rest of the year, from November to February.
Le palais royal et l’arbre généalogique: The Royal Palace and the Gbaguidi family tree
La grotte de Kpataba, refuge des habitan: The Kpataba Cave, a refuge for the local people during raids
Le marché et ses huiles de palme: The market and its palm oils
Des dômes de granit sortent de la plaine: Granite outcrops rise up from the plain all around the town — the Savè Hills, which have become a small climbing area. The River Ouémé flows right past them.
Novembre à février : la roche est sèche: November to February: the rock is dry and the air is clearer.
Les dômes granitiques et la vue depuis l: The granite domes and the view from the summit
Le marché, sur l’axe Cotonou–Parakou: The market, on the Cotonou–Parakou route
La plus vaste commune du pays, étirée le: The country’s largest municipality, stretching along the Northern Road. Visitors stop off here for the roadside market, the rice fields of Bétérou and the banks of the Ouémé.
D’octobre à décembre, juste après les pl: From October to December, just after the rains: everything is green.
Le marché de Tchaourou, au bord de la na: The market in Tchaourou, on the edge of the main road
Les berges de l’Ouémé, spectaculaires en: The banks of the Ouémé, spectacular at low water
Un village accroché au flanc de la colli: A village clinging to the hillside, made up of round mud huts with thatched roofs, each topped with an upturned pot. The Taneka have maintained a highly structured initiation system there: one ascends with a guide from the village.
Novembre à février. Guide du village obl: November to February. A village guide is compulsory; visitors are not allowed to explore on their own.
La montée dans le village et ses cases c: The climb up to the village and its conical huts
Les forgerons, caste à part et respectée: Blacksmiths: a distinct and respected caste
Les prêtres traditionnels et le bois sac: Traditional priests and the sacred wood — see box
La vue sur la plaine depuis le haut du v: The view of the plain from the top of the village
La ville-carrefour au pied de l’Atacora,: The crossroads town at the foot of the Atacora, nestled between cliffs and gorges. This is where you enter the Pendjari, and the road leading up to it is a sight to behold in its own right.
De décembre à avril, la saison des parcs: From December to April: the park season.
La route des gorges, vers la Pendjari: The Gorges Road, towards the Pendjari
Les chutes de Yéripao, à une vingtaine d: The Yéripao Waterfalls, about twenty kilometres away
Le marché, très animé le jour de foire: The market, which is very lively on market day
L’hôpital Saint-Jean-de-Dieu, connu dans: The Saint-Jean-de-Dieu Hospital, renowned throughout the sub-region
L’aéroport international Cardinal-Bernar: Cardinal Bernardin Gantin International Airport is the country’s gateway. It is situated in Cotonou itself, just a few minutes from the ocean: for many, the journey begins here, in the heat that hits you as soon as you step off the jet bridge.
Toute l’année. Les vols long-courriers p: All year round. Long-haul flights mainly depart in the evening.
Le change et la carte SIM, à régler avan: Currency exchange and SIM card – to be sorted out before leaving the lobby
Les taxis et les zémidjans à la sortie —: Taxis and zémidjans at the exit — the fare is agreed before you get in
La plage de Fidjrossè, à un quart d’heur: Fidjrossè beach, a quarter of an hour away
Le poumon économique du pays, et le débo: The country’s economic powerhouse and the maritime gateway for the entire Sahel region: a large proportion of goods from Niger and Burkina Faso pass through its docks. This is also where containers shipped from abroad arrive.
Toute l’année. Le port ne se visite pas: All year round. The harbour is not open to the public: it can be viewed from the marina.
Les grues et les porte-conteneurs, vus d: Cranes and container ships, as seen from Boulevard de la Marina
Le port de pêche voisin, à l’aube, quand: The nearby fishing harbour at dawn, when the boats come in
Le départ de la route qui monte vers le: The start of the road leading up towards the River Niger
Sur la route des royaumes: On the Road to the Kingdoms
L’axe, du port au fleuve: The route, from the harbour to the river
Du port au fleuve: From the harbour to the river
La mémoire, les palais, la Porte du Non-: Memory, the palaces, the Gate of No Return.
Le cordon littoral, le lac Nokoué et le: The coastal strip, Lake Nokoué and Lake Ahémé — you get around by pirogue.
L’Atacora, les tata somba, les cascades: The Atacora, the tata somba, the waterfalls and the two parks.
La route qui monte de Cotonou jusqu’au N: The road that winds its way up from Cotonou to Niger, from market to market.
